title: Betting on Lower Oil Prices? Consider These Inverse ETFs

description: Oil prices have declined significantly from October highs as Goldman Sachs and the IEA forecast a potential global oil supply surplus. title: Where These 4 Sector ETFs Stand Heading Into Year-End
author: James Brumley
description: As 2026 winds down, the article analyzes four key sector ETFs heading into 2027. Technology stocks have pulled back 14% from October highs after AI companies missed earnings, but the sector remains reasonably valued. Financial stocks are mixed, with insurance outperforming while banks struggle amid tepid loan demand. Energy stocks surged 40% YTD on oil prices but face headwinds as crude may have peaked around $90/barrel. Healthcare stocks are up 21% but appear slightly overvalued at current levels.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recent 14% pullback from October highs is viewed as a healthy reset to more reasonable valuations. Forward P/E of just above 20 is considered reasonable, and AI technology still has practical value despite near-term volatility.
Mixed performance with insurance stocks performing well due to higher interest rates, while banks struggle with tepid loan demand. Selective approach recommended rather than broad sector investment.

While up 40% YTD, the sector faces headwinds in 2027 as oil prices near $90/barrel resistance level. EIA predicts crude will average around $80 in 2027, and alternatives to oil are expanding, limiting upside potential.

Despite 21% YTD gains, the ETF is slightly overvalued with forward P/E above 22 and overbought technical conditions. Market may be pricing in results unlikely to materialize until 2028, suggesting a pullback is warranted.

title: Markets Are Pricing in a Fed Rate Hike in December. Here's What Investors Should Do, According to History.
author: Keith Speights
description: Markets are pricing in an 81.2% probability of a Fed rate hike in December 2026. Historical data shows the S&P 500 typically rises ~9% in the year following a new rate-hike cycle, despite initial short-term declines. Investors should avoid panic selling, favor energy stocks, shift to short-duration bonds, and monitor the Fed's dot plot for clues about future rate hike aggressiveness.

author: Na
description: Oil prices are projected to stay high in 2027 due to Middle East tensions, damaged energy infrastructure requiring years to repair, OPEC production discipline, and uneven refinery recovery. title: Should You Invest in the iShares U.S. Energy ETF (IYE)?
author: Na
description: The iShares U.S. Energy ETF (IYE) is a passively managed fund with $1.76 billion in assets, offering broad exposure to the energy sector with a low expense ratio of 0.37%. The fund has performed strongly, gaining 43.44% year-to-date and 47.77% over the past year, but carries higher risk with a standard deviation of 21.28%. Top holdings include ExxonMobil (23.59%), Chevron, and ConocoPhillips. The fund received a Zacks ETF Rank of 3 (Hold), with alternatives like Vanguard Energy Index Fund (VDE) and State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) offering lower expense ratios.
